section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the interpretation placing "and her captives in charity" above "Zion shall be redeemed through justice" aligns with the explanation in Likkutei Torah and the Arizal's writings, where justice repels external forces from the point of Zion, but charity is needed to return her to her original place, being beyond the line of strict law.
section.t: And behold, this interpretation—that the aspect of "and her captives in charity" is higher than the aspect of "Zion shall be redeemed through justice"—corresponds with the explanation in Likkutei Torah and in the writings of the Arizal13 on the verse "Zion shall be redeemed through justice."
[Except that there he explains the two aspects on a lower level,]

for Zion is the point of Zion, the Yesod of Nukva, and because it is hollow and the lights are revealed there, that is where the external forces have a hold. Therefore it says that through justice etc., they cause it to be redeemed and drive away the external forces from there.

But all this is only so that they should not take hold of her alone, and she will be recognizable there in her place, but she has not yet ascended to her first place and emerged from among them completely.

However, in order to remove her from among them and to elevate her and seat her in her first place, one must perform charity etc. And this is "and her captives in charity"—to return her to her place requires charity, and through the merit of charity she will return to her first place.
Thus, "and her captives in charity" is higher than "Zion shall be redeemed through justice."
And this is also understood simply,
as it is written there,
that justice
(although justice is mercy14)
its essence is according to the line of law,
unlike charity, which is beyond the line of law.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the interpretation where "and her captives in charity" is lower than "Zion shall be redeemed through justice" is connected to the higher interpretation, like a reversible seal, and elaborates on the future superiority of action over study, the transition from the Tabernacle (vegetative) to the Temple (mineral), and the elevation of Yehudah (the inanimate) above Yosef (the vegetative).
section.t: And behold, it is explained elsewhere15 that interpretations of a single verse are related to each other.
From this it is understood

that the interpretation that "and her captives in charity" is lower than "Zion shall be redeemed through justice" has a connection to the interpretation that "and her captives in charity" is higher than "Zion shall be redeemed through justice."
(And it is in the manner of the known concept16 of a reversible seal.)
And the explanation is as follows:
It is known17 that our Sages, of blessed memory, said:18 "Study is great now, but in the days of Moshiach, action will be great."
Now, study and action correspond to the vegetative and the inanimate,
and in the future, action will be great,
for then the superiority of the inanimate will be revealed.
And this is in the manner explained19 on the verse "And Yehudah approached him," regarding the difference between the Mishkan and the Beis HaMikdash
[This matter has a special connection to Shabbos Chazon,
and as the R' Hillel of Paritch wrote:20
And the depth of this matter will be explained
(that on Shabbos Chazon, the future Beis HaMikdash is shown to each person)
with what is explained elsewhere regarding the matter of "And Yehudah approached him," the history of our Temple etc.].
That the Mishkan was made of shittim wood,
cedars,
the vegetative,
unlike the Beis HaMikdash, which was specifically made of stones and earth
(and it is forbidden to have protruding wood in it, etc., as it is written:21 "You shall not plant for yourself an asherah, any tree").
Because in the Beis HaMikdash there was a revelation of the superiority of the inanimate.
And the main revelation of the superiority of the inanimate will be in the future
(in the third Beis HaMikdash),
when Yehudah
(the aspect of the inanimate)
will be elevated to be above Yosef
(the aspect of the vegetative),

as it is written:22 "Behold, I will take the stick of Yosef... and I will place them upon him, the stick of Yehudah... and My servant Dovid shall be king over them... and My servant Dovid shall be their prince forever."23
For this is also what is meant by "in the future, action will be great,"
because the essence of Dovid is action,24
and as explained elsewhere25 regarding the difference between Dovid and Yehonasan
(Malchus and Yesod, corresponding to Yehudah and Yosef)
the son of Shaul,
that Yehonasan the son of Shaul is the matter of study
(his service was according to Torah and mitzvos, unlike "to obey is better than sacrifice"
(the aspect of Dovid)),
and it is said, "Shaul from Rechovos HaNahar,"
for "Rechovos HaNahar" is the matter of understanding and comprehension,
study,
and Dovid is the aspect of action.
And it is said, "Until Dovid, he magnified."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that even now, although study is great, there are matters where action is superior, such as performing a mitzvah that cannot be done by others, and that the emphasis on action now is because all future revelations depend on our actions during exile, as explained in the Alter Rebbe's letter about the primacy of charity in the era of Moshiach's footsteps.
section.t: And behold, although now study is great,
nevertheless there are several matters
(even now)
in which action is superior to study.
For example, that one suspends Torah study for a mitzvah that cannot be performed by others.26
And the content of Igeres HaKodesh, beginning "Hu v'Chayohi"
[which was written by the Alter Rebbe in the village of Poyena in the days before his passing27]
is about the superiority of practical mitzvos.

And the reason that even now they emphasize the superiority of action can be explained as follows: because all the revelations of the future depend on our actions and service throughout the entire time of exile,28
and since in the future action will be great,
therefore even now they emphasize the superiority of action,
for through this the revelation of the future will come, when action will be great.
And in the manner explained in Igeres HaKodesh,29
that our Sages, of blessed memory, did not say "Torah study is equivalent to all the mitzvos" except in their days, but in these times, at the heels of Moshiach,
the primary service of G-d is the service of charity.
